messages:
AcmeCorp: hitting 403 after onboarding — key shows up in console but their service calls return 403. ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/6789
Chris (Customer Success): thanks for flagging, assigning to support. can you paste the exact curl and response?
AcmeCorp: sure — repro from their env:
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_ABC123" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'
```
response: HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"project_scope_mismatch"}
Dana (Support): ok. can you confirm the project id shown in the console for that key? and whether they used the project-scoped key or org-wide token?
AcmeCorp: console shows project id: proj_9876. they say they used the key from the project page.
provisioner-bot: provisioner event: 2025-11-01T14:00:10Z created api_key sk_live_ABC123 bound_to: temp-internal-project-456 claim_status: claimed
provisioner-bot: claim binding event: 2025-11-01T14:00:11Z attempted bind to proj_9876 -> failed, bound to fallback project temp-internal-project-456
Devon (Provisioning): looks like provisioner fallback logic kicked in — binding race. if claim not present at bind time we stick to fallback internal project.
Chris (Customer Success): partial repro from our side: quick repro by creating account + immediate key request sometimes maps to temp project.
Dana (Support): can we confirm this is why the key returns insufficient_scope? i.e., console shows proj_9876 because UI later resolved, but key was bound to temp-internal-project-456 with different allowed scopes?
Morgan (Infra): confirmed. the temp-internal-project has restricted scopes (internal-testing) so API rejects calls requiring prod scopes.
Devon (Provisioning): workaround for customer: rotate the API key from the console (regen). new key creation will trigger provisioner bind after tenant claim has propagated. that should bind correctly to proj_9876.
AcmeCorp: regen worked, new key returns 200. can you patch so others don't hit this?
Devon (Provisioning): root cause: provisioner attempts bind before tenant_claim_event processed if claim latency > ~500ms. fallback behavior is to bind to internal test project. plan: change fallback to hold and retry bind for up to 5s, and add idempotent reconcile job to rebind keys when claim shows up.
Morgan (Infra): will also add a short-lived alert when keys are bound to any temp-internal-project to catch regressions.
Dana (Support): I'll send customer a note with repro steps and workaround (regen key).
Chris (Customer Success): ETA on fix?
Devon (Provisioning): PR ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/412 — change bind order + retry loop. landing to staging now, aiming for prod deploy in next maintenance window (2025-11-02 02:00 UTC).
Morgan (Infra): staging deploy ok, rolling to prod in 30m. will monitor for alert spikes.
Devon (Provisioning): post-deploy note: running reconcile for keys bound to temp-internal-project-456. will rebind any mismatches to their proper project.
provisioner-bot: reconcile job started: 12 keys queued, 1 already resolved, 11 reprovision tasks in flight.
AcmeCorp: thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
Dana (Support): marking ticket 6789 as resolved after confirm from customer. closing once we see no further 403s in 24h.
Chris (Customer Success): adding follow-up to run a short audit of keys created in last 24h to ensure no more temp bindings.
Dana (Support): noted.
Morgan (Infra): postmortem slot created for this in "postmortems" channel, will include mitigation and timeline.
AcmeCorp: confirmed stable.
